title: Which trades help

D0.outcome: Explains that a trade has a purpose and lists the purposes (open a file, destroy a defender, relieve cramp, simplify when ahead).

D1.outcome: Given a position and a possible trade, names which purpose it serves, or says it serves none.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, chooses between trading and keeping the tension, including cases where trading helps the opponent (it relieves a cramp) or trades off his own good piece.

D3.outcome: Predicts how a trade changes structure and game phase, avoids trading a piece that has moved several times for one that has not, and checks the resulting ending before trading when ahead.

misconceptions: Any exchange that relieves tension is good.
An exchange that fits none of the listed motives is bad (too absolute).
conditions: The trade serves a purpose: open a file without losing a tempo, destroy a defender, avoid retreating, simplify when ahead, settle a key point.
If ahead, trade into an ending that is theoretically won; avoid pawn structures that lose endings.
contrasts: A trade that relieves the cramped side; fewer pieces help the cramped side.
'only the listed motives justify a trade' is overstated; modern play also trades for structure or the bishop pair.
A trade that is forced anyway, or in a position decided by a tactic.
